title: Millennials and the Takeoff of Craft Brands: Preference Formation in the U.S. Beer Industry
authors: Bart J. Bronnenberg; Jean‐Pierre Dubé; Joonhwi Joo
eligible_reason: Not a binary staggered DiD. Main reduced-form tables regress household craft-beer purchase on generation cohort dummies, education, income and household size, plus continuous local craft availability (avail, availY_21after1979), with scantrack (and in some columns panel_year) FE; IV versions (ivreghdfe) instrument availability with population and years since brewpub legalization (yearsLegal/years, a continuous exposure). The remaining results are a structural preference-formation model (MATLAB GMM). No binary treatment switching on at unit-specific dates enters any reported regression.
design_notes: Stata (r2-r5), R (r1, r6 figures), MATLAB (r7 structural). Nielsen Homescan/RMS household-year data, American Breweriana Association brewery entry data, state brewpub legalization years (lawsStateYear.dta). Cluster gg.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: generation cohort dummies and continuous availability with demographic controls; IV with population and years-since-legalization instruments

data_files_note: No data files shipped; master_readme points to Nielsen-Kilts Homescan/RMS (licensed), American Breweriana Association, Elzinga et al. (2015), ratebeer.com and public SEER/Census data. Only make.log outputs are included.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex metadata (no article text). Brewpub legalization dates vary by state but enter only as a continuous years-since-legal instrument/regressor, not as a DiD treatment.
